summary: Tested the new Google Places-backed Find-a-Lawyer feature. Backend (6/6 pytest passed) and Frontend (all critical flows verified: postcode fallback, sponsored-first, via-Google badges, Google-result detail with Open-in-Maps + no inquiry form + disclaimer, sponsored-result detail with inquiry form + successful submission).

tests_executed.backend_pytest: 6/6 passed — sponsored+google merge, postcode resolved_address, 400 on missing params, dedupe (no double Crown & Bench), 24h cache fast on repeat (<800ms), legacy /api/lawfirms regression OK
tests_executed.frontend_playwright: Verified: sign-in -> dashboard -> tile-lawyers opens lawyers-modal, geolocation denied -> postcode fallback (SW1A 1AA), 21 cards rendered (1 sponsored + 20 google), Crown & Bench Solicitors top with Sponsored pill + distance '2.69 km away', 20 'via Google' badges, Google-result detail has data-testid='open-in-maps' (href contains 'google'), inq-name absent, 'Listed via Google Maps' disclaimer visible. Sponsored detail has inq-name + send-inquiry-btn; submitting inquiry returned 'Message sent — Crown & Bench Solicitors will get back to you soon.'

not_fully_tested_due_to_script_state: Radius selector re-fetch and 'All firms' tab click after inquiry success — script tried while modal was still on the 'Message sent' confirmation. Code review confirms tabs render when !selected and All-tab fetches legacy /api/lawfirms which already passed backend regression. Low risk.
critical_code_review_comments: /app/frontend/src/App.js is ~16k lines — strongly recommend splitting LawyersModal and other large components into separate files (file-size rule >700 lines).

_PLACES_CACHE is an in-process dict — fine for a single-pod deployment, but if backend scales horizontally each pod will hit Google independently. Consider Redis or sharing via Mongo with TTL for production scale.

Cache key buckets to ~1.1km grid but radius is part of key — two callers with radius_km=10 vs 20 at the same bucket re-hit Google. Acceptable given 24h TTL, but consider keeping the largest radius response and filtering client-side.
Dedupe matches only by normalised name; two firms with the same name in different cities could be merged incorrectly. Consider name+postcode hash for stronger dedupe.

success_rate.frontend: ~95% (all critical assertions passed; tab-all + radius re-test skipped due to script state)

context_for_next_testing_agent: GOOGLE_PLACES_API_KEY is live in /app/backend/.env and Places API (New) v1 endpoints (searchNearby + searchText) are working against the user's GCP project. Quick smoke: curl 'http://localhost:8001/api/lawfirms/nearby?lat=51.5074&lng=-0.1278&radius_km=10' should return ~21 results with Crown & Bench Solicitors first.
